full_judgment:
2. The suit was filed seeking declaration that the order dated June 30. 1983 passed by defendant No.1, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Rangpur in Miscellaneous Case No.37 of 1981-82 declaring the land appertaining to RS Khatian No.7 as khas land is void, illegal, inoperative and without jurisdiction. 

 3. The suit was tiled averring that the land in suit measuring 3.30 acres of CS khatian No.6, corresponding the RS khatian No.7, belonged to Bibi Ummat Johara and others and the said landlords settled the land in suit with Bipin Chandra in 1350 BS by granting Dakhila, that said settlement holder Bipin Chandra possessed the land in suit upon payment of rent to the ex-landlords, that RS record was prepared in the name of Bipin Chandra, that Bipin Chandra sold the land in suit to the plaintiff on February 27, 1970, that the plaintiff got his name mutated and possessed the land on payment of rent, that Bipin Chandra in collusing with others filed criminal cases against the plaintiff but he was acquitted. that defendant No.2 filed Title Suit No. 170 of 1980 claiming easement right over the suit land but the same was dismissed for default, that Bipin Chandra filed Title Suit No. 428 of 1979 impleading the plaintiff but later on the same was withdrawn and he tiled fresh suit being No. 159 of 1982 seeking cancellation of the kabala on the basis of which plaintiff claiming the land in suit but the said suit was disposed of in favour of the plaintiff that Bipin Chandra through the defendant No. 2 managed to tile Miscellaneous Case No.37 of 1981-82 before the defendant No.1 tor cancellation of the mutation made in favour of the plaintiff, that defendant No.1 illegally cancelled on June 30, 1983 the mutation which was made in the name of the plaintiff on the view that the land claimed by the plaintiff on the basis of the kabala dated February 27, 1970 is the khas land, that land of the RS khatian No.7 (corresponding to CS Khatian No. 6) was not government khas land and that plaintiff's vendor since settlement from the ex-landlords possessed the land purchased by him on February 27, 1970 and that since purchase plaintiff is in possession of the land in suit, that since the order of the defendant No.1 cancelling the mutation is illegal hence the suit seeking the relief of declaring order of the defendant No.1 illegal void and without jurisdiction. 

 4. The suit was contested by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by filing separate written statements. The common case of the defendants was that prior to preparation of CS khatian land of the suit plot was being used as Eidgah, Swashan, Debesthan and that there is a Dighi for the use of the people of the village, that in the CS khatian there is noting that in the plots in question there are Eidgah, Swashan, etc., that there is similar noting in the RS record, that since the acquisition of rent receiving interest of the landlord. the land in suit is being used by the public in general (Muslims and Hindus) for the purposes as mentioned hereinbefore, that Bipin Chandra in collusion with the settlement personnel got the RS record prepared in his name although there was no basis for the preparation of the RS record in his name since Bipin Chandra had never taken settlement from the ex-landlord, that as Bipin Chandra had no right. title, interest and possession in the land in suit, the plaintiff by his so-called purchase did not acquire any interest in the land in suit, that neither Bipin Chandra nor the plaintiff possessed the land in suit, that defendant No.2 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 50 of 1978-79 before the defendant No.1 and the same was decided in favour of the defendant No.2 and the order in the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case was not challenged by Bipin Chandra or by the plaintiff, that Miscellaneous Case No. 50 of 1978-79 was tiled as regard the land of plot Nos. 259 and 34 since the land of those two plots were Swashan, that defendant No.2 later on filed Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 1981-82 before the defendant No.1, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Rangpur and the said defendant by the order dated June 30, 1983 quite legally cancelled the mutation earlier made in the name of the plaintiff in respect of the land in suit. 

 6. The plaintiff went on appeal. The appellate Court reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court primarily on the finding that defendant No. 1 has no jurisdiction to cancel the record of right. It is seen from the judgment of the appellate Court that the said Court proceeded upon the assumption that settlement of the land in suit to Bipin Chandra was not disputed by the defendants and that Bipin Chandra paid rent to the landlord, although the consistent case of the defendants was that there was no settlement of the land in suit by the landlords to Bipin Chandra and that no paper was brought on record in support of the claim that the land in suit was settled with Bipin Chandra by the landlords and Bipin Chandra paid rent to the landlords. The appellate Court, without discussing at all the evidence, arrived at the finding that Bipin Chandra on taking settlement possessed the land in suit and the plaintiff after his purchase possessed the land in suit, that provision of section 143 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act does not authorise the Revenue Officer "to correct Khatians which affects the question of title or possession to land. It has power only to correct Khatian if it has been made as a result of bonafide mistake...............Moreover, revenue officer cannot declare a document to be void". The appellate Court also observed that the defendant No.1 in cancelling the mutation went beyond the limit of his power and the order so passed by the defendant No.1 was without jurisdiction. The appellate Court further observed "I am of the view that if Government thinks that the lands in question belong to or the same are in actual occupation of Hindu Community they should seek redress in the civil Court in an appropriate forum and not in this capricious manner". 

 8. The defendant No.2 moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained the Rule. The High Court Division in the background of the evidence, both oral and documentary, as well as other materials on record, was of the view, as the trial Court was of, that Bipin Chandra did not acquire any title on the basis of his alleged settlement and the RS record prepared in the name of Bipin Chandra had no basis since from plaintiff's side fact of Bipin Chandra's taking settlement was not established either by documentary evidence or by oral evidence. The High Court Division was also of the view similar to that of the trial Court that the plaintiff did not acquire any right, title and interest in the land in suit since his vendor Bipin Chandra did not acquire any right, title and interest in the land in suit. The High Court Division also held since plaintiff had no title in the land in suit, the mutation in the name of the plaintiff was not legal and thus cancellation thereof by the defendant No. 1 was quite legal. The High Court Division while making the Rule absolute observed "Unless the plaintiff proves his title to the suit land he is not permitted to challenge the order of the ADC (Rev) Rangpur. The lower appellate Court has not reversed the finding of the trial Court that the plaintiff acquired no title on the basis of his kabala from Bipin as Bipin had no title to the suit land. The plaintiff 'Could not produce any paper showing settlement in favour of Bipin by ex-landlord Ummat Zohora and others. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties submits that the order of Mutation was passed under section 117 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and an appeal lies against the said order within 30 days which was not filed by the defendant. Section 117 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act relates to Sub-Division of holding and restriction thereon. Mutation proceeding and Sub-division of holding are not identical. Mutation of the khatian or correction of the Khatian may be made by the Revenue Officer on application by interested party or of his own motion under section 50 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the ADC (Rev) Rangpur has the jurisdiction to correct the mistakes appearing in the revenue record committed by the Revenue Officer on bonafide mistake. Accordingly, the ADC (Rev) Rangpur had the jurisdiction to correct the record relating to the khatian which was mutated in the name of the plaintiff by the Upazila Revenue Officer. When it is found that the plaintiff has no title to the suit land, the mutation of the suit land cannot stand in the name of the plaintiff The lower appellate Court therefore committed an error of law in reversing the decision of the trial Court without considering the plaintiff's title to the suit land. The impugned judgment and decree therefore, suffer from illegality and infirmity and cannot be sustained".
